findings.message: `optin` treats an existing `fleet:auto` tag as consent no matter who added it. If the item is assigned to the caller and already tagged, it exits 10 (no-op). If the item is unassigned and already tagged, it only adds the assignee and keeps the tag as it is. The trigger/dispatch consent gate requires `fleet:auto` to have been added *by the assignee*, so both variants report success but leave an item the gate refuses. `optin_plan` (`lib/optin.sh:10`) and status's `not-opted-in` logic make the same assumption. Fix: when the tag is present but the caller is not the one who added it, remove and re-add the tag in the same rev-guarded PATCH (or refuse with a clear message). Add a variant test for both shapes.
findings.scenario: Unassigned WI #209 tagged `fleet:auto` by bob. Alice runs `specclaw-fleet optin 002-a`, which prints `opted in (#209, assigned to alice…, fleet:auto)` and exits 0. Status shows the item opted in. `specclaw-fleet trigger 002-a` then exits 4: `fleet:auto was not added by the assignee`. The same happens when the item is assigned to Alice and the tag was added by Bob: `already opted in` exits 0, then trigger exits 4.

findings.message: `--since` is accepted as any string and compared lexicographically against `createdDate` with the fraction stripped (`…Z`). A value with an offset, a fraction or a missing `Z` gives silently wrong filtering. Validate it as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, or normalise it (e.g. through `date -u`), and fail on anything else.
findings.scenario: `status 002-a --watch 30 --since 2026-11-08T10:00:00+05:30` (that is 04:30Z) with a `pr_open` record at `2026-11-08T04:40:00.1Z`. The string comparison `"2026-11-08T04:40:00Z" >= "2026-11-08T10:00:00+05:30"` is false, so the row shows `waiting` and the watch never ends.

findings.message: `terminal` only knows run ends that wrote a record or a `fleet:refused` tag. A run that ends without posting a record never becomes terminal, so `--watch` loops forever. Two such runs: the Job is killed by `activeDeadlineSeconds` or OOM before the entrypoint posts `failed`, or the pipeline step errors before launch. The row already has the newest Job's phase. Treat `cluster.phase == "failed"` as terminal when that Job was created after `--since`, which needs `creationTimestamp` in the `status_job` output.
findings.scenario: Trigger 002-a. The Job hits its deadline and the pod is killed, so no `failed` comment is posted. `status 002-a --watch 30 --since <t>` shows `cluster: fleet-002-… failed/Failed` and `record: waiting`, and it re-renders indefinitely.

findings.message: `load_fleet_settings` reads the local working-tree `.specclaw/config.yaml` before `trigger` runs. So trigger's credential gate checks the vault from local, unpushed config. The pipeline it queues reads `fleet.vault` (and image, claude_version, namespace) from the pushed commit. The two can disagree, which is the same class as the earlier trigger/FETCH_HEAD lesson. The setup skill even writes config and then asks before pushing. Fix: in `trigger`, load the `fleet:` settings from the FETCH_HEAD `config.yaml` it already extracts (keeping env and flag overrides). Alternatively, refuse when the local and pushed `fleet:` blocks differ.
findings.scenario: Setup writes `fleet.vault: kv-new` locally and does not push it, while `origin/main` has no `fleet:` block. `specclaw-fleet trigger 002-a` passes the credential gate against kv-new and queues the pipeline (exit 0). The pipeline's checkout has no vault, so dispatch fails with `No Key Vault`, and the operator watches a run that the gate reported as passing.

findings.message: `status_pipeline` shows `run: ?` both when the pipeline lookup failed and when AzDO answered that no pipeline has that name. Distinguish `missing` from `unknown` in the header.

The key regex `^[[:space:]]+([a-z_]+):` accepts lines at any depth, so a nested map under `fleet:` (e.g. `  extra:\n    vault: x`) has its inner keys loaded as top-level fleet settings. Match exactly one indentation level (the first key's indent) and warn on deeper lines.

The doc says `--watch` returns once every change is `pr_open` or `failed`. The code also ends on a `refused` record, a `fleet:refused` tag, `not-opted-in` and `no work item`. Align the doc with the code.
